paragraphs.text: Scores every DSH tool call with a local Ollama decision model before it runs - risky calls become an
approval prompt, an unreachable model stops everything.
# dsh-ollama-tool-guard
**A second opinion on every tool call your DeepSeek Harness agent makes — from a model running on yo
n on every tool call your DeepSeek Harness agent makes — from a model running on your own machine.**
Your agent can read any file, run any command and fetch any URL the sandbox allows. This plugin puts
a small local model in front of each call. Ordinary ones pass silently. Risky ones come back to you
as an approval prompt that says what the model thinks the call does and whether it acts inside or o
utside your workspace.
If the model cannot be reached, nothing runs. The guard fails closed rather than letting calls slip
not be reached, nothing runs. The guard fails closed rather than letting calls slip past unreviewed.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x
- Ollama 0.35.1 or newer (0.40.6+ if you use a `:cloud` model) — this uses

its System One decision API
- About 6 GB of disk for the default model
## Install
**1. Pull the model** (once, ~6 GB):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**2. Install the plugin:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**3. Restart `dsh web`.**
**4. Open Settings → Plugins → Tool guard.**
If the plugin does not appear under Settings, add `"dsh-ollama-tool-guard"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`
in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` and restart again — installing the package and registering it
as a bundle are two separate steps.
## What you will see
When a call is surfaced, the prompt reads like a sentence:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Left to right: what the model believes the call does (`READING`, `WRITING`, `MODIFYING`, `DELETING`,
`SYSTEM CHANGE`), whether it acts inside or outside your workspace, why it was flagged in plain wor
ds, then the tool and a short summary. Approve to run it, reject to block it. Nothing runs while the
l and a short summary. Approve to run it, reject to block it. Nothing runs while the prompt is open.
Everything is adjustable while the harness runs — **Settings → Plugins → Tool Guard**. Changes apply
to the next call, no restart:
## Choosing a model
The judge is whatever your own Ollama serves. Any decision model works; these three are the ones thi
s was built against:
| `model` | Runs on | Size | What leaves your machine |

| `clef-flash` *(default)* | your GPU | 9B, ~6 GB | nothing — fast enough for a per-call gate |
| `c

lef` | your GPU | 27B, ~18–20 GB | nothing — the more careful local option |
| `clef:cloud` | Ollama
's provider | — | each reviewed call |
Change it in **Settings → Plugins → Tool guard → Connection**. The **Test saved config** button send
s one probe question and reports the latency, or exactly what went wrong.
## What leaves your machine
With the default local model: nothing. Every review is a request to your own Ollama, so command line
s, file contents and URLs stay on the box. A `:cloud` tag sends each reviewed call to the provider i
contents and URLs stay on the box. A `:cloud` tag sends each reviewed call to the provider instead.
The audit log records what was decided, never the text of the call. See SECURITY.md for the full pic
ture, including the gaps.
## Where things live

| Config | `~/.dsh/tool-guard.json` — re-read on every call, so edits apply immediately |
| Audit lo

g | `~/.dsh/tool-guard-audit.jsonl` — one line per call |
| Settings | **Settings → Plugins → Tool g
uard** — model, endpoint, thresholds, effect classes, test button |
## If something goes wrong
| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| Every tool call is denied | The guard cannot reach its model. Check `ollama list` has the model pu
lled, and that the endpoint in Settings is right. The denial message names the model and the fix. |
| `the user rejected tool "…"` and you were never asked | The session has no approval surface — a de
legated or headless run, or prompts disabled. Use `skip` or `enabled: false` for unattended work. |
| Prompts on things you find harmless | Raise the matching threshold, or untick the effect class in

Settings. The prompt tells you which rule fired. |
| Plugin code changes do not apply | The host cac
hes modules. Restart `dsh web`. |
